blocking_unknown: The single remaining blocker is the loader's pointer-RELOCATION TABLE (finding igz.loader.relocation-table). A record's class/vtable is assigned for every record in the enumerated span, but its pointer FIELDS are rebased from an explicit relocation table, not from the record bytes: a clone whose pointers were hand-rebased in the file is still not fixed up (owner->physics link stays a raw offset, so the child is built at a bogus address and the load hangs). Registering the clone by growing the header table shifts every object 32 bytes and desynchronises the relocation globally (froze after 1 036 of 21 680 records). The relocation table (159 245 entries, runs of consecutive pointer words) is not stored verbatim as offsets/cumsum/bitmap/byte- or u16-delta in any section, so it must first be located and decoded, then the clone's new pointer-word offsets inserted and later entries shifted. This is a distinct decode task.
mechanism_found: Why a valid appended IGZ object is not instantiated: (1) the loader does not walk section 1 sequentially, does not use the header table as a construction root and does not use the section-0 table as a size stream; it constructs a contiguous span of records and each record builds its embedded children (findings igz.loader.enumerated-span, igz.loader.pointer-traversal). (2) An object appended after the last record is outside the span and stays raw bytes (never constructed) — the cause of the first M3 failure. (3) Loading applies a fixup pass: section-indexed pointers (igz.pointer.section-indexed), class pointers, id remap, reference counts (igz.object.refcount); section 5 is a second object section with 2 320 pointers into section 1 (igz.section5.object-section).
positive_results: The game tolerates an appended object, a grown LZMA chunk table and a modified section-1 header table (loads, plays)
